name: April 28, 2026 Regular Meeting
minutes_text:
Minutes
  Lakewood City Council
  Regular Meeting held
  April 28, 2026

MEETING WAS CALLED TO ORDER at 7:31 p.m. by Mayor Chase in the Council Chambers at
the Civic Center, 5000 Clark Avenue, Lakewood, California.

INVOCATION
was offered by Dr. Fardad Mogharabi, Spiritual Assembly of the Baháʼís of Lakewood

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE
was led by Girl Scouts Troops 113 & 3433

ROLL CALL:
PRESENT:  Mayor Cassandra Chase
  Vice Mayor Jeff Wood
  Council Member David Arellano
  Council Member Steve Croft
  Council Member Todd Rogers
.  .  .

ANNOUNCEMENTS AND PRESENTATIONS:

Mayor Chase 1) provided details relative to the traffic calming pilot program installed on
Studebaker Road near Rynerson park, explaining a) the program is the result of an extensive
study, including a traffic calming evaluation, which was driven by ongoing concerns of
speeding, unsafe driving and pedestrian access in the area; and b) temporary materials have
been utilized to evaluate how it functions, further noting that staff have been on-site monitoring
the conditions to determine if modifications are needed; 2) highlighted that three hundred
volunteers participated in the 29th Annual Lakewood Volunteer Day; 3) recognized Lakewood
resident, Aida Lansangan, on her 100th birthday; 4) reported on her attendance at the
a) Lakewood Youth Sports Coaches Recognition event; b) YMCA Youth in Government
Recognition event; and c) Cal Cities Leaders Summit; and 5) noted that as the President of the
Cal Cities Women’s Caucus, she hosted a conversation on childcare as infrastructure.

Vice Mayor Wood 1) recognized Norma Lopez as this year’s Older Adult Volunteer of the
Year; 2) noted that he joined Council Member Arellano in presenting a certificate to City of
Paramount’s Mayor, Brenda Olmos, for her year as President of the California Contract Cities
Association; 3) highlighted the grand opening of Zoo Spicy Bistro located at 2450 E.
Carson Street; 4) reported on his attendance at the a) Volunteer Day work sites;
b) Volunteer Day Application Luncheon; c) Aida Lansangan’s 100th birthday party;
d) Lakewood Youth Sports (LYS) Coaches Recognition; and e) Water Walk Event held at
Lakewood High School; 5) stated that the last home game for the Lakewood High School
baseball team will be held on May 5, 2026, further noting that this will be the last game for
long-time Coach Spud O’Neil; and 6) recognized Deputy City Manger Beltran for being
selected by California State University Long Beach as a “49 under 49” honoree which is a

prestigious award that recognizes the dedication, excellence and impact of alumni through their
professional achievements.

ANNOUNCEMENTS AND PRESENTATIONS - Continued

Council Member Croft reported on his attendance at the OneLegacy Donate Life Run/Walk
event held on April 25, 2026.

Council Member Rogers 1) provided details relative to the traffic calming pilot program
installed on Studebaker Road near Rynerson park, stating a) traffic safety is a top concern
amongst the residents; b) the City is required to meet the State of California traffic
requirements; c) temporary materials have been utilized with the intent to monitor and evaluate
its function, further thanking staff for their efforts on the implementation and evaluation of the
program; 2) stated he is aware of the increased number of “youth bike mobs” in the community,
noting that the City is developing strategies and implementing measures to alleviate the issues;
3) highlighted that Goodwill will be opening at the former Joann Fabrics & Crafts store located
on Lakewood Boulevard and Candlewood Street; 4) explained that the City is bound by state
law with regard to the building of Accessory Dwelling Units (ADUs); however, the City is
continuing to work on minimizing the impacts of ADUs; and 5) noted that the demolition and
remediation on Lakewood Boulevard and South Street has begun.

Council Member Arellano 1) commended staff for their efforts on the future development on
Lakewood Boulevard and South Street; and 2) reiterated that he is aware of the increased
number of “youth bike mobs” in the community, further encouraging residents to contact the
City and/or law enforcement if an incident occurs.

For the record, Mayor Chase introduced Captain Dan Holguin, Lakewood Sheriff’s Station,
who provided a verbal report pertaining to Part 1 crimes from January 1, 2026, to
March 31, 2026.

At the request of Council Member Rogers and Council Member Arellano, Captain Holguin
1) confirmed that there is a shortage of Los Angeles County Sheriff Deputies at the Lakewood
Sheriff’s Station; however, academy classes are fully funded and eighteen trainees recently
filled vacant positions at the station; 2) stated that Deputies are mandated to work six overtime
shifts per month; 3) explained that the Los Angeles County Sheriff’s Department is working
with the City Manager, Director of Public Safety, District Attorney, and School Districts in the
City of Lakewood on enforcement of the youth bicycle mobs, noting that an education
campaign will be conducted; and 4) confirmed that he will look into the possibility of
beautifying the lobby at the Lakewood Sheriff’s Station.
  .  .  .

PUBLIC COMMENT ON ITEMS IN THE AGENDA - None
  .  .  .

2.1 • SECOND READING AND ADOPTION OF ORDINANCE NO. 2026-4;
AMENDING THE LAKEWOOD MUNICIPAL CODE PERTAINING TO PROVISIONS
FOR THRIFT STORES AND AMENDING VARIOUS PROVISIONS OF CHAPTER 3
ARTICLE IX (DEFINITIONS) INCLUDING AN EXEMPTION FROM THE
CALIFORNIA ENVIRONMENTAL QUALITY ACT (CEQA) PER CEQA GUIDELINES
SECTION 15061(b)(3)

Deputy City Attorney Skolnik introduced the item.

For the record, Council Member Arellano reiterated that the City does not have the authority
to prevent a thrift store from opening next to an established thrift store, further stating that
though residents may not favor a specific business opening at a location, the occupancy of a
vacant building can prevent homelessness.

Following discussion, it was moved by Vice Mayor Wood, seconded by
Council Member Rogers, and unanimously carried by the following roll call vote, to adopt
Ordinance No. 2026-4:

AYES: COUNCIL MEMBERS – Wood, Croft, Arellano, Rogers, and Mayor Chase
  .  .  .

3.1 • QUARTERLY BUDGET REPORT OF MAJOR FUNDS – AS OF MARCH 31,
2026

Mayor Chase introduced the item.

Director of Finance and Administrative Services Gomez provided a PowerPoint presentation
of the Agenda report.

For the record, Council Member Arellano expressed gratitude for the work conducted by staff.

For the record, and without objection, the report was received and filed.
  .  .  .

3.2 • AUTHORIZE ADDITIONAL CONTRACT AUTHORITY AND APPROPRIATION
OF GENERAL FUNDS FOR BLOOMFIELD PLAYGROUND IMPROVEMENTS
(PW 2024-04)

Mayor Chase introduced the item.

Director of Public Works Pickler provided a verbal report of the Agenda report.

For the record, Council Member Croft stated that the Capital Improvement Program Committee
recommended approval of the additional contract authority and appropriation of general funds
for Bloomfield Playground Improvements.

For the record, it was moved by Council Member Croft, seconded by Vice Mayor Wood, and
unanimously carried by the following roll call vote, to 1) appropriate $110,000 in
General Funds to support the additional work; and 2) authorize an increase in contract authority
for Public Works Contract No. 2024-04 with Micon Construction Inc. in the amount of
$171,734 and authorize staff to execute the change order for removal and replacement of the
existing poured-in-place rubberized surfacing at Rynerson Playground:

AYES: COUNCIL MEMBERS – Wood, Croft, Arellano, Rogers, and Mayor Chase
  .  .  .

3.3 • PAN AM FIESTA PREVIEW

Mayor Chase introduced the item.

Director of Recreation and Community Services Frost provided a PowerPoint presentation of
the Agenda report.

For the record, and without objection, the report was received and filed.
  .  .  .

LAKEWOOD HOUSING SUCCESSOR AGENCY

1 • REGISTER OF DEMANDS

It was moved by Council Member Rogers, seconded by Council Member Arellano, and
unanimously carried by the following roll call vote, to approve the register of demands:

AYES: COUNCIL MEMBERS – Wood, Croft, Arellano, Rogers, and Mayor Chase
  .  .  .

ORAL COMMUNICATIONS:

Mary Alice McLocghlin, resident, and Jamie Tarantini, resident, spoke regarding feral cat
concerns and requested that the City of Lakewood 1) fund a voucher program for residents to
get cats spayed and 2) support trap-neuter-return programs that some residents were currently
organizing and funding themselves.

In response to the comments provided by Mary Alice McLocghlin and Jamie Tarantini, Mayor
Chase suggested they speak with Deputy City Manager Beltran.

Ben Chavez, resident, 1) expressed gratitude for new crosswalks; 2) shared his concerns
regarding traffic and parking in his neighborhood; 3) discussed speed bumps in Long Beach;
and 4) inquired about trash and water for ADUs.

In response to the comments provided by Ben Chavez, Mayor Chase suggested he speak with
Public Works Director Pickler.

Philip Norris, resident, 1) discussed street sweeping citations; 2) suggested law enforcement
utilize residential security cameras; 3) inquired about a handicap ramp at Carson Street and the
605 freeway; and 4) noted that feral cats helped lower rat populations.

In response to the comments provided by Philip Norris, Mayor Chase suggested he speak with
Public Safety Director Yordt.

  .  .  .

ADJOURNMENT
There being no further business to be brought before the City Council, Mayor Chase adjourned
the meeting at 8:53 p.m.

Respectfully submitted,

Isabelle Schultz, CMC
Assistant City Clerk
